Compact Sets

This scene tests compactness with open covers. See whether finitely many covering pieces always suffice.

Compact means closed and bounded together. An open end needs endless pieces near the gap. An endless stretch fails the same way. With both conditions, any cover shrinks to finitely many pieces.

For example, cover a desk completely with 📚 books. A finite desk needs only a few books. An endless desk would defeat any pile, however large.

K compact   ⟺  K closed and boundedK \text{ compact } \iff K \text{ closed and bounded}K compact ⟺K closed and bounded

This is the engine of the Extreme Value Theorem (the evt scene) — for continuous fff on [0,1][0,1][0,1], the set f([0,1])f([0,1])f([0,1]) is compact, hence closed and bounded in R\mathbb{R}R, so its supremum and infimum are actually attained.
